candidates.desc: In a Ghibli-style animation, a woman slides her card into a street ATM at night, types her PIN, takes the banknotes from the lit tray and her card back, then buys a bouquet of sunflowers with the cash.

In a packed country hall a young woman raises her numbered paddle again and again, bidding against the crowd on an antique chest and a grandfather clock while the auctioneer's gavel falls; she wins and hugs her paddle.

A waiter places a folded restaurant bill on a plate; the couple unfolds it and it turns out comically long, the woman gasps and laughs, then the man counts out a thick stack of dollar notes onto the plate and they pay cheerfully.

At an outdoor flea market, a young man skeptically examines a gold ring an old woman seller is offering him. He turns it over, squints at it against the light, frowns, says he does not think so, and puts the ring back on the stall table unconvinced.

In an office a desk fan blows sheets off a paper stack while two coworkers scramble; the woman takes a paperclip from a glass dish, clips the stack together, and the papers now hold even in front of the fan as they celebrate.

In a Pixar-style office a nervous young man slides his green passport to an immigration officer and asks to enter. She checks the pages, sticks a colorful visa into the passport and stamps it. He raises his fist and thanks her, delighted.

In a concrete parking garage a man in a navy suit runs his hand slowly along the bonnet of a bright red sports car. He opens the door and lowers himself into the red leather seat, then reaches for the start button on the steering wheel and the dials light up. The car rolls out of the garage with its headlights on, and the last shot shows it standing alone in profile on an empty rooftop deck under a grey sky.

A woman in a white shirt and grey cardigan sits at a desk buried under thick stacks of receipts and invoices, lit by a desk lamp at night. She frowns over a long till receipt held up in one hand, runs a red pen down a ruled ledger full of columns of figures, circles one number in red, taps the big black calculator, and finally throws both fists in the air in triumph.

An estate agent in a green blazer with a lanyard and a folder opens the door of an empty flat and waves a young couple in; she pulls the sheer white curtains aside and opens the balcony door onto a city skyline, and the three of them stand looking out; in the hallway she hands the couple a set of keys and they laugh with delight.

A woman in a bright floral dress stands on a sunny city street holding up two big brown paper shopping bags, one in each hand, grinning. She then walks through a shopping centre past lit storefronts with bags hanging off both arms, adds more bags and totes, and finally rides up an escalator hugging a pile of paper bags to her chest.

A woman in a dark suit pushes through the glass doors of a bank. At the counter a clerk feeds banknotes through a counting machine. She then walks into the wide marble entrance hall, a big information screen on the wall and a row of staffed desks along the side. At the back a man in a suit turns the wheel of the huge round steel door and she stares into the corridor of deposit boxes behind it.

A large bearded man in a white shirt sits in a busy open-plan office with a telephone handset wedged against his ear. His desk is buried under printed forms and official papers, many of them already marked with big red crosses. He grabs a sheet, slams a rubber stamp down on it and leaves a red X across it, then bangs the stamp onto the ledger in front of him again and again, getting angrier until sheets of paper are flying up all around his head.

A busy diner with red vinyl booths, white tablecloths and a violinist playing between the tables. An elderly woman in a grey suit sits at a booth and slides a folded napkin across the cloth. A man in a blue shirt and tie with a gold watch heaves a brown leather briefcase up onto the table opposite her. The two of them then sit behind raised menus, glancing sideways at each other. The camera pulls back to show the long tablecloth is draped over a wheelbarrow parked at the table, and under the cloth the barrow is heaped with banded bundles of cash; they reach across and shake hands over it.

At a money-changer's booth in a busy covered bazaar, a moustached man in a grey shirt and dark waistcoat holds out a thick bundle of banknotes in both hands over a glass case. He counts through a stack of purple notes, then spreads dozens of notes into a wide fan across the counter, laying different currencies side by side. A young woman in an orange beanie watches with her mouth open in amazement, and at the end he passes a handful of notes over to a hand reaching in from the camera side.

In a bright office a woman with short white hair in a blue suit leans over a desk and spreads a printed document on a clipboard in front of a young man in a suit, pointing at the line where he has to sign. He takes a pen and signs it. They stand up, she puts a hand on his shoulder and they shake hands while the staff at the desks behind clap. At the end she leads him to a free desk with a small box marked Welcome on it, and the whole office applauds.

A close shot shows a hand writing a name into a spiral-bound book headed REGISTRATION, with other names already filled in. Two smiling staff in lanyards hand a printed name badge across the counter to a guest. Behind the desk more staff work with stacks of forms, badge printers and card scanners while a queue waits. The camera pulls back to show an enormous convention hall with a huge crowd lined up at long check-in tables.

A young man in glasses and a cardigan sits at a metal cafe table by the sea, writing on the back of a picture postcard with a blue biro; a stamp lies on the table beside it. He then stands at a rotating rack of postcards on a village street, turning it and pulling out a fan of cards. Finally he stands at a yellow street postbox, holds the postcard to his lips, pushes it through the slot and pats the box.

A postman in a bright red high-visibility uniform and red cap wheels a red bicycle along a street of English terraced houses; a red bag stuffed with letters hangs from the handlebars. He pushes a bundle of letters through the letter slot of a red front door, knocks on the door, waves to a woman watering her front garden, hands a wrapped birthday parcel over a brick garden wall to a resident, then rides off smiling at the camera.

A grey-haired woman in a burgundy suit steps out of a black limousine onto a red carpet in front of a white palace lined with flags and guards and waves to the cameras, then sits at a desk and signs a document with a black fountain pen, holds the open folder up to show the fresh blue signature, and finally raises both arms to a cheering crowd from a balcony.

A young woman in a beige coat and orange beret shops her way through a city: first in a wood-panelled chocolate shop where she holds up a chocolate bar, then at a clothes rail where she takes down an olive coat, then at the till where she hands the coat over and pays at the card terminal, then walking through the glass atrium of a shopping centre, and finally out through the doors holding a large white gift bag tied with a gold ribbon.

A man in a dark suit sits at a polished wooden desk in a grand hall with EU and French flags behind him and writes a looping signature on a sheet of paper with a gold fountain pen. He works through a tall stack of pages, lifting each one as he signs. Then two aides unroll an enormous roll of paper the whole length of the table, and while photographers film he leans over it and signs it with an oversized pen.

An open-plan office. A woman in a rust-coloured blouse sits at a desk with a corded handset wedged against her ear, talking into it while she reaches for a pink sticky note and taps at her keyboard. Around her the desk fills up with towers of loose printed sheets and ring binders - one stack to her left, another rising in front of the monitor, more piling up until they reach above her head and box her in. Colleagues move about in the background. She stops, puts the handset down and slumps forward onto the desk between the paper towers.

In a dark theatre lit by warm lamps, a laughing young woman holds a cream envelope up to the camera; the flap is closed with a round red wax seal pressed with a stamp. A young man in a green hoodie then shakes his hands in front of his chest and pulls a wide-eyed, nervous face. The shot cuts to a group of young people on a lit stage who jump, scream, hug each other and celebrate.

A man with a moustache in a brown corduroy jacket and a striped shoulder bag stands at a shop checkout, pulling a blue bank card out of a brown leather wallet next to the card terminal. He then walks through an open-air fruit market and opens the same wallet in front of the fruit crates, searching through it. He lifts the wallet up to the camera with both hands and turns it around so the empty pockets show, grinning in disbelief. Finally he leans over a wooden table where a small pile of loose coins has been tipped out, and pushes the coins around with both hands while another person's hand reaches in from the other side.

A young woman with a black bob sits at a wooden desk by a bright window, a green cardigan on, tapping a black fountain pen against her lips while she thinks over a sheet of writing paper. She then writes a handwritten letter across the page, folds the finished sheet, slides it into a cream envelope and presses the flap down flat with both hands. In the last shot she stands in the street at a red pillar postbox, smiling as she pushes the envelope through the slot.

The point of view of a customer at a white marble café counter: two forearms in blue sleeves with thin gold bracelets push a small spread of coins together into a pile. Behind the counter a young man with a beard, in a white shirt and a dark apron, leans on his elbows and watches the coins with a thinking face, then counts on his fingers and grins. A tall brass coffee urn with an eagle on top, a glass dome of macarons, a small espresso cup and an espresso machine stand around him under globe lamps.

Seen from an official sitting at a wooden desk in a vaulted hall of red brick and pale stone, his left hand with a steel watch rests on a document on a leather folder while his other hand presses a wooden rubber stamp onto it and lifts it, leaving a round red mark. Across the desk a young woman in a mustard top and cream trousers clasps her hands to her chest and smiles with relief and joy. A tabby cat gets up and stretches across the desk towards the document while the stamp comes down again. A glass of tea and a brass lantern are nearby.

In a bright room, close beside the heavy carved gold edge of an old painting, a young man with curly dark hair, wearing white cotton gloves, holds a small magnifying loupe to his eye and studies the canvas closely. A young woman in a green satin blouse leans in beside him and shines a small torch at it. Then he lowers the loupe and says something to her, she gasps with surprise and laughs with a hand on her chest, and they smile at each other. An antique wooden cabinet stands behind them.

Under the glass roof of an outdoor flower market at dusk, on wet pavement, a young woman with sunglasses on her head, in a camel jacket and dark jeans, holds out a banknote to a stallholder and takes a large bunch of pink and red dahlias. She hugs the flowers to her chest and walks away towards the camera, smiling. Metal buckets of flowers stand on the ground and hang above, hanging scales dangle from the stall roof, rolls of wrapping paper are fixed to the counter and a woman waits behind her.

In an elegant old office with wooden cabinets, a checked black and white floor, green banker's lamps and a crystal chandelier, an official in a dark jacket and gold watch presses a heavy brass embossing seal onto a cream certificate with a gold seal and a red ribbon on a round walnut desk. A smiling young woman with long black hair, in a green cardigan, sits across the desk with her chin on her hands, watching. The official then lifts the certificate and holds it up to her, and she looks at it in delight.

In an elegant restaurant in the evening, with chandeliers, candles, white tablecloths and tall arched windows over a river, a young woman in a green silk dress looks down into her open brown wallet with a nervous smile. A man in a velvet jacket points happily at the menu while a waiter pours champagne. She closes the wallet in her lap and looks up as a waiter brings a tall three-level tray of lobster, crabs and oysters to the table, and she smiles. A violinist plays behind them.

In an old-fashioned bank office with tall windows and a large leather-topped desk with a brass lamp, a serious young woman in a dark grey suit sits at the desk and slides a folded paper towards a bearded man in a cap sitting opposite her. He picks it up and unfolds it while she holds a pen. Behind her a man in a dark suit reads a big open ledger, and a heavy steel vault door stands open, showing shelves stacked with bundles of banknotes.

On a snowy city street at night, a young woman with long braids, a white bobble hat, black gloves and a sparkly silver sequinned coat stands at a cash machine set into a stone wall, taking banknotes from it while the screen glows. She puts one hand in her pocket and turns towards the people in winter coats queuing behind her, one of whom holds up a card. Streetlights, falling snowflakes, a paper cup on the pavement and a shop window with fairy lights fill the background.

In an office at night with glass towers outside the window, a young woman with long curly hair, round glasses and a cream blouse sits at a desk and checks a thick stack of printed financial accounts, circling a number with a red pen. Three young men in shirts lean over her shoulders to watch; then they straighten up, one rubs his face and one drinks from a coffee cup. She looks up, smiles and goes back to the page. Piles of papers, binders, a calculator with a paper roll and a noodle box surround her.

A young woman with long black hair and a mustard cardigan sits at a wooden desk by a window over a rainy garden, laughing as she writes a letter with a fountain pen. A pressed pink flower lies on an open envelope, and next to it is a thick bundle of airmail envelopes with colourful stamps tied with a ribbon. She lifts the pen to her lips, smiles and writes on. A bottle of ink, a mug of tea and a stand with a handwritten letter are on the desk, and a cat sleeps on the window seat.

A wood-panelled auction room. A young woman with braided hair, a cream blazer and white gloves sits at a green table and holds up a sparkling cut diamond with tweezers into a beam of sunlight, turning it and sending rainbow sparkles across the room, then smiles. A black tray of rings lies in front of her. Behind a rope barrier the audience watches, a woman laughing and a man shielding his eyes from the glare, while a guard in a dark suit and white gloves stands by.

At a busy street market on a wet cobbled square, a young woman with long braids and a camel coat crouches beside crates of onions and potatoes and writes on a clipboard with a small line graph drawn on it. She looks up thoughtfully, taps her pen against her chin and goes on writing. A chalkboard next to her shows the prices of potatoes and onions per kilo. Above her an older trader in a flat cap and apron holds out an onion, and a hanging scale and customers fill the back under striped awnings.

In an old wood-panelled lawyer's office on a rainy day, a young woman with messy red hair held up by pencils, in a paint-splashed denim jacket, sits at a leather-topped desk with her hands at her open mouth in shock. An old man slides a big ring of old iron keys and a worn leather folder towards her. She grabs the keys, lifts them up and stares at them with a huge excited smile. Behind her, relatives in black suits and dresses stare in disbelief, one man getting up, beside a grandfather clock and shelves of law books.

An old lost property office. A young woman with a blond bun, a dark blue shirt and waistcoat stands behind a worn wooden counter and hands one small single item, a tiny white object wrapped in tissue, into the open palm of a customer reaching in from the left. She places it in the hand, the customer pulls back, and she folds her hands and smiles. Tall shelves behind her hold umbrellas, bicycles, crutches and stuffed birds. A man carries a tuba in the background, and a ticket book and a brass bell lie on the counter.

In the gravel courtyard of a large stone villa among vineyard hills, a man with slicked-back hair, an open cream silk shirt, gold chains, black trousers and loafers strides across a white towel laid over a puddle and keeps walking towards the viewer. Four young women in white blouses and black trousers follow him in a line, carrying expensive leather handbags, one holding a small dachshund in a bag. Classic silver sports cars are parked by a stone fountain, and tall cypress trees stand by the courtyard.

A wet street of tall stone terraced houses on a sunny autumn day with yellow leaves blowing about. A black dog in a red postman's cap and red uniform stands on its back legs at a round red pillar postbox and empties the letters from its open door into a big canvas mail sack. It then drops onto all fours and trots off with the sack on its back towards a small red mail van at the kerb, where a black and white collie leans out of the window and watches.

Friends sit at a long wooden counter in a noodle bar, seen through the eyes of one of them, whose hands in blue sleeves push banknotes onto a big pile of money in the middle. A young woman in a rust jumper lays down another note, a smiling man in a white T-shirt drops in coins, and a young woman in a pink top throws her arm up and cheers. The hands in blue sleeves pull back and then gather the pile together. Empty noodle bowls and glasses of water stand around it, and cooks work behind the counter.
